name: DeepSpeed-FastGen: High-throughput Text Generation for LLMs via MII and DeepSpeed-Inference
problem: Existing frameworks force a choice between throughput and latency for LLM generation, and this hurts most with long prompts where the prefill phase dominates.
mechanism: Dynamic SplitFuse: decompose each request into prompt and generation work, then compose the split so prefill for the next request overlaps generation of the current one, with the split point chosen dynamically per request rather than fixed.
speedup_reported: Per the arXiv abstract, versus state-of-the-art systems LIKE vLLM: up to 2.3x higher effective throughput, 2x lower average latency, and up to 3.7x lower token-level tail latency, for long-prompt generation workloads. The system is built by combining DeepSpeed-MII with DeepSpeed-Inference. Reported across various models and hardware configurations; read the paper's benchmarking methodology section for the exact settings, since long-prompt effective throughput is highly sensitive to prompt length.
notes:
VENUE NOT VERIFIED — arXiv comment is empty and I found no proceedings record; recorded as arxiv-preprint deliberately. Adoption in-production but with a caveat worth stating: FastGen ships as a mode in DeepSpeed-MII, which is deployed inside Azure and other Microsoft stacks, yet DeepSpeed's serving path has clearly lost ground to vLLM/SGLang in the open-source ecosystem. Dynamic SplitFuse is the same family of idea as Sarathi-Serve chunked prefill and was developed independently.
